papers.title: Multimodal prediction of MCI-to-dementia conversion over a two-year window.
papers.reason: The study predicts clinically important cognitive decline using multimodal data, but the title provides no indication of executive-function tasks, eye tracking, EEG, or process modelling.

papers.title: Quantitative analysis of intersecting pentagon drawings for interpretable cognitive impairment screening.
papers.reason: Quantitative and interpretable analysis of a drawing task is directly relevant to behavioral digital screening for cognitive impairment, although no multimodal or executive-process analysis is specified.

papers.title: Diagnostic accuracy of the ADAS-Cog-13 as a cognitive screening tool in older adults with focal epilepsy: A multicenter cross-sectional study.
papers.reason: This evaluates a general cognitive screening instrument in a clinical population without a stated focus on executive-function mechanisms or digital and multimodal biomarkers.

papers.title: A Harmonized Visual Reading Framework for Tau PET Staging in Alzheimer Disease.
papers.reason: The framework improves early Alzheimer pathology staging and relates tau burden to global cognition, but it does not specifically investigate executive function or behavioral, eye-tracking, or EEG assessment.

papers.title: Association of MIR137 rs1625579 polymorphisms with cognitive function in patients with untreated first-episode depression.
papers.reason: The paper links a genetic polymorphism to cognition in depression, but the available title does not establish a specific finding about planning, working memory, attention, or cognitive control.

papers.title: Preliminary validation of Cogniclear: a virtual reality cognitive screening tool for older adults against the Montreal Cognitive Assessment
papers.reason: The study validates an immersive cognitive assessment using continuous behavioral interaction measures and domain-level comparisons with MoCA, providing a relevant digital assessment methodology despite its small preliminary sample.

papers.title: Serum BDNF and cognitive risk in maintenance hemodialysis: a machine learning study
papers.reason: The study predicts MoCA-defined cognitive impairment from serum and clinical variables, but it does not model executive processes or use the behavioral, eye-tracking, and EEG modalities of primary interest.

papers.title: ARLC-Net: An Adaptive Representation Learning Framework for Electroencephalography-Based Brain Age Clustering
papers.reason: The paper analyzes age-related EEG spectral and functional-connectivity patterns in human datasets, but its main contribution is a clustering method rather than findings or models specific to executive function.

papers.title: Evaluation of Visuospatial Ability in Elderly Adults Using Eye Tracking and Virtual Reality Content
papers.reason: This is a close methodological match using a VR task, eye-tracking-derived quantitative features, and classification of healthy older adults versus participants suspected of MCI for early cognitive screening.
